changes: New groupMessageCache helper derives group-v1 SHA-256 tags from group/message/author/device/key-epoch/ciphertext context. Identical timestamps and ciphertext lengths do not alias different edits. This is cache identity, NOT sender authentication or cryptographic conversation binding.

Group batch decryption requires matching cache scope and source tag, and sufficient stored file keys for attachment messages. Send/edit/decrypt cache writes preserve source tags and encrypted attachment keys; own-device and attachment-only messages can reopen without replaying already-consumed Signal envelopes.

Additive optional encryptedSourceTag/fileKeys fields use the existing IndexedDB object store. No schema bump, blanket cache deletion or production migration. Same-scope unedited legacy originals can be upgraded without replaying Signal; this compatibility path relies on the existing unedited server metadata and is not advertised as authenticity verification.

Edited/mismatched legacy entries are left intact. If the current encrypted version cannot actually open, content and stale file keys are withheld and a localized version-unavailable explanation is shown. Old cached plaintext is never relabeled as a successfully decrypted edit.

Per-message freshness guards prevent an old history item from overwriting a newer edit's persistent cache while other valid items in the batch continue. Cache-write failure does not discard a successfully decrypted body or attachment keys.

Encrypted recovery backup export/import preserves the additive cache fields. Existing backup version/algorithm and old optional-field compatibility remain unchanged; no plaintext network path was introduced.
verification: 6 focused files / 124 tests passed; correct tsc -b and targeted ESLint passed. Initial typecheck caught a test mock returning null where the real Signal decrypt API returns string/throws; changed the test to model a real decrypt failure rather than weakening types.
Full client regression after cache changes: 222 files / 2091 tests passed in 45.64s. Existing jsdom navigation warnings were not suppressed.

Encrypted recovery follow-up: keyBackup suite 20 tests passed in 11.31s. The existing real AES-GCM/PBKDF2 round-trip now restores version tags and file keys into an empty cache, so existing-cache priority cannot mask dropped backup fields. TypeScript and targeted lint also passed after the follow-up.
Real SHA-256 tests vary same-length ciphertext and source context while proving timestamp-only changes do not invalidate an identical encrypted version.

Tests cover exact-version own-device attachment cache reuse, same-timestamp edits, wrong-conversation cache entries, legacy original upgrade, unavailable legacy edit, per-item supersession, attachment-only empty text, cache-write failure and real IndexedDB field round-trip.

Local Vite production web build passed (1646 modules, 683ms). Existing config-loader, chunk-size and ineffective-dynamic-import warnings remain. No Windows packaging or production publication was performed.
remaining: Actual two-client/device edit delivery, offline/reconnect, recovery and attachment playback acceptance remains unperformed; browser space remains handed to the user.

An edited legacy record without a source fingerprint cannot always be safely matched or re-decrypted after Signal state was consumed. Its old data is preserved, but availability of that latest version is not guaranteed and is explicitly explained.
Broader Signal/session account-lifecycle isolation, cryptographic conversation binding and concurrent session-write validation remain separate incomplete gates; cache hashing does not prove them.

Known partial attachment-upload results and original key ordering were subsequently implemented (p4-group-partial-uploads-2026-10-24.json). Unknown network commit outcomes and real file acceptance remain open. Pre-edit draft backup/restore was also implemented (p4-group-edit-drafts-2026-10-24.json); this does not close P4 or overall acceptance.
